body:
Currently in the shader docs, "constant" is used loosely. It refers to:
- Values marked with `const` which exist in global scope (that is, outside of the vertex, fragment, and light functions): https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/shaders/shader_reference/shading_language.html#constants
- "Global built-in constants" like PI: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/shaders/shader_reference/spatial_shader.html#global-built-ins
- literal values that are not marked `const`: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/shaders/shader_reference/shading_language.html#casting
  > Default integer constants are signed, so casting is always needed to convert to unsigned

All of these seem fine to refer to colloquially as "constants", but I would be in favor of referring to the third case as "literals" instead. I think there are only a few places in the docs that would need to be changed in this case.

If in doubt, I think we should be following GLSL terminology, since Godot's shading language is mostly based on GLSL.

(This also needs an opinion from someone involved with the shader compiler, though)

Taking a crack at a PR for this currently. "Constant" is a little overloaded in the language tokenizing/lexing and I'm seeing if I can sort of tease out if renaming is appropriate in some cases (as well as fixing the error strings).
